feasible.reason:
The defect SE-03 describes is real and live, but the proposed fix does not stop the stated attacker, so it is refuted as written; a different firmware-only fix should replace it.

Why the confirmation probe fails: the probe proves the SCP03 session is alive, not that the card issued the verdict. An interposer forwards CreateSession (or VERIFY) to the card untouched and replaces only the response with a bare `69 86` (or `69 85`). The host advances its counter on the bare status word (secure/src/se050/scp03.rs:614-634) and the card advanced its own when it processed the command, so both stay in sync. The follow-up GetRandom/ReadObjectAttributes then returns a valid R-MAC'd response and the forged verdict is promoted to `AuthMethodBlocked`, then wipe. A genuinely locked card produces the identical transcript (bare 0x6986, then a healthy probe), so the two cases cannot be told apart. This follows from the protocol: error status words are never R-MAC'd, so a negative verdict cannot be authenticated by any later command. The only authenticated source would be an R-MAC'd positive read of the UserID attempt attribute, which the production policy denies with a bare 0x6986 (CLAUDE.md invariant #2).

The secondary goal, "an interposer can only DoS, never destroy", is also unreachable as proposed. `gated_unlock` precharges page 124 before the SE call and never refunds on `InternalError` (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1473-1491, 1601-1631). Ten induced failures reach MAX, the next call returns `PinLocked` (mod.rs:1445-1454), and `cmd_request_unlock` wipes (secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-163). "Do not charge page 124 on inconclusive" would need a refund path, which conflicts with the precharge-before-verify FI design and gives a glitch attacker free retries.

No board change is needed either way; this stays firmware-only.
feasible.corrections:
1. Replace the mechanism. Make MCU page 124 the only wipe authority, since it is the only authentic local state. Map an SE-reported lockout (`Se050Error::AuthMethodBlocked`, and the OPTIGA `PinLocked` arms that derive from unauthenticated status or readback) to a non-wiping "SE locked / transport fault" state, as the boot and PendSV arms already do (secure/src/main.rs:4198-4205, 4587-4595). Offer the wipe only behind an explicit trusted-UI confirmation. This is S to M firmware and removes the one-shot forged wipe.

2. An authenticated lockout verdict needs a different SE050 policy. The UserID attempt attribute would have to be readable under R-MAC, which means a policy change, re-provisioning and a silicon decision (CLAUDE.md invariant #2 calls this "separately reviewed"). The proposal's own risk note concedes the probe target is unvalidated; in fact no probe target can work.

3. Correct the threat statement. In the dual-SE shipping shape, SE050 is consulted only when OPTIGA returned Ok or PinIncorrect, and an OPTIGA error wins (secure/src/dual_se.rs:370-392). So a forged SE050 0x6986 wipes only when the user typed the correct PIN, and only through CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK. "Zero attempt budget consumed" is accurate; "any PIN" is not.

4. The forged-0x6985 half adds little. Page 124 is already charged before the SE call, and any transport fault leaves it charged. The real residual is ten induced faults leading to a wipe, which the proposal does not close.

5. "Escalate to lock after N inconclusive" needs a new durable counter. That is allowed (it is not per-signature state) but should be folded into page 124 semantics rather than a second counter that can drift (the paired-constants hazard).

6. The Trezor precedent is overstated. core/embed/sec/tropic/tropic.c:183-186 `is_retryable` retries on `LT_L1_CHIP_ALARM_MODE`, `LT_HAL_ERROR`, `LT_L2_IN_CRC_ERR` and `LT_L2_CRC_ERR`, then restarts and re-opens the session (lines 190-216; init retry at 1404-1411). That is a transport-error retry list. It contains no "never retry a possibly-executed command" rule (a HAL error can follow execution) and nothing about authenticating negative verdicts. Cite it only for "restart and re-establish the session on a transport fault". The Ledger LSB-016 claim was not checked.

7. Priority and cost. P0 is too high: the attack needs an opened device with an implant on I2C4 (PB6/PB7), it is destructive but not confidentiality-breaking, and funds are recoverable from the 24 words. P1 fits. Cost S holds for the corrected "no SE-driven wipe" design; the proposal as written (probe, inconclusive class, durable counter, OPTIGA leg, silicon validation) is M.

8. Not checked: the cited issue numbers (#104, #105, #106, #120, #168, #385) and the "brick is permanent on the current SE050" claim.

live_defect.evidence: secure/src/se050/scp03.rs:614-634: a 2-byte response is copied out, the counter is advanced and Ok(2) returned with no MAC check. secure/src/se050/apdu.rs:385-395 turns that status word into Se050Error::Status(sw). apdu.rs:768 (create_session) and :845 (verify_session) map 0x6986 to AuthMethodBlocked. secure/src/se050/mod.rs:2865-2871 and 3027-3048 map that to UnlockError::PinLocked. secure/src/dual_se.rs:395-403 propagates it. secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1626-1631 passes the error through gated_unlock. secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-163 calls trigger_lockout_wipe, which runs factory_reset_admin and pin_attempts_reset (190-211). None of these steps is behind a dev or test cfg.
live_defect.reachable_in_production_config: Yes in code. The path is unconditional under se050 + dual-se, both of which are in RELEASE_FEATURES and PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2662, 2718). Two limits apply. It fires only via NSC CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK; the boot and PendSV unlock arms show 'PIN locked / power cycle' and do not wipe (secure/src/main.rs:4198-4205, 4587-4595). And because OPTIGA's error takes precedence (secure/src/dual_se.rs:370-392), the user must have entered the correct PIN. A mode-production + optiga-trust-m image cannot be built today (OPTIGA_S2_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED fence, secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:315), so the path has only been exercised in bench dual-SE builds with the same code.
live_defect.severity: Medium. A physical implant or interposer on the SE050 I2C4 bus forces a one-shot dual-SE wipe on the next correct-PIN unlock over USB, without consuming attempt budget. It is destructive, with no key disclosure and no signing-authority gain; funds are recoverable from the seed words. An accidental bus glitch producing exactly 69 86 in a well-formed T=1 frame is implausible, so this is an adversarial case only.

already-have.reason:
SE-03 is not implemented, but its core is already tracked by open issues #104/#105/#106/#120, so it is not refuted — it is a consolidation of tracked work with a small untracked delta.

Task 1 (implemented?): No. On the SE050 side every cited step is live as described:
- `unwrap_response` still returns a bare 2-byte SW as `Ok(2)` with no authentication tag (secure/src/se050/scp03.rs:615-635).
- `create_session` maps 0x6986 to `AuthMethodBlocked` (secure/src/se050/apdu.rs:768); `verify_session` maps 0x6985/0x63xx to `PinIncorrect` (:824) and 0x6986 to `AuthMethodBlocked` (:845).
- `classify_se050_unlock_error` maps `AuthMethodBlocked` to `PinLocked` (secure/src/se050/mod.rs:2865-2871).
- The gateway wipes on `PinLocked` with no corroboration (secure/src/nsc/cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-164), and `trigger_lockout_wipe` discards the wipe result (:205).
- `authenticate_and_read` propagates a `create_session` error with `?` and no retry; it only calls `reinit()` after a failed verify, then returns the same error (secure/src/se050/mod.rs:2763-2793).

Two fragments exist. Commit 255a9554 (#715) added `PENDSV_MAX_NO_VERDICT_FAILURES = 3` (secure/src/main.rs:4466), a consecutive-verdictless cap that stops without wiping; I confirmed it only at the PendSV re-unlock site and found no equivalent in `cmd_request_unlock.rs`, and per its doc comment it still burns page 124 on each failure. D1 (d33bba58, per #385) made `Se050Error::Transport` inconclusive (secure/src/se050/apdu.rs:24-27, 77-95), but that same doc classes `Status`/`PinIncorrect`/`AuthMethodBlocked` as authoritative "because the SE spoke" — the assumption SE-03 challenges.

Task 3 (decision conflicts): it changes the invariant #2 wipe mapping and re-litigates the 2026-09-21 choice to keep page 124 charged on errors; both are listed in decision_conflicts. Neither is an owner "do not re-raise" decision, and #104/#105 are standing evidence, so this is tension rather than contradiction.

Task 4 (repo_evidence): the four code citations are accurate today and all four cited issues are OPEN. The one stale premise is the OPTIGA leg, detailed in corrections.
already-have.corrections:
1. Reframe as an implementation plan for existing issues. SE-03 is mostly #104 + #105 + #120 with a different fix shape. #104 proposes: reject bare SW in {0x9000, 0x62xx, 0x63xx}, and corroborate `AuthMethodBlocked` across `reinit()` plus a fresh session plus a page-124 floor before wiping. #105 proposes: bare 0x6985 is inconclusive; only authenticated 0x63Cx is a PIN failure.

2. The OPTIGA leg rests on a stale premise. #120's body cites a global `0x0E → PinLocked` / `0x07 → PinIncorrect` mapping in `parse_response`. The doc comment at secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:303-317 says those per-reason `Sta` arms were dead code on real silicon and are from "an earlier revision"; `PinLocked` now comes from the E120 pre-check (secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:2432, 2454, 2474, 2480, mapped at :3190) and the verify site collapses `Status(_)` to `PinIncorrect`. I read the comment and the grep hits, not the `parse_response` body. The live OPTIGA concern looks closer to #125 (verdict confusion; :2474 turns a counter read-back failure into `PinLocked`). I did not check whether the E120 read is under Shielded Connection. Re-scope this leg to #125 plus an authenticated E120 read.

3. The confirmation probe may not close the attack — treat as a reasoned concern, not checked against GP Amd D or silicon. An R-MAC'd reply to a later probe shows the channel is live then; it does not authenticate the earlier bare SW. An interposer can forge one frame and pass the probe through. A genuine wrong-PIN or locked verdict is plausibly itself a bare error SW, so #105's "only authenticated 0x63Cx" may be unobtainable. The corroboration that looks sound is (a) the page-124 floor already named in #104 (refuse to wipe on `AuthMethodBlocked` while MCU-local page 124 is well below MAX, or require the verdict to repeat across a hard reset and fresh session), and (b) lock-not-wipe escalation. Production SE050 policy denies attribute reads (CLAUDE.md invariant #2), so the probe target is constrained, as the proposal's own risks note.

4. "Do not charge page-124" needs restating. Page 124 is precharged before the SE call (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1474), so this means a refund. A refund triggered by an attacker-forgeable bare SW is a free PIN-probe oracle against the MCU counter. Follow the 255a9554 shape instead: keep the charge and cap consecutive verdictless results.

5. 0x6983 maps to nothing: no occurrence under secure/src/se050/. Drop it or justify it.

6. "The only [wipe] an attacker with just bus access can trigger today" is overstated: #106, #125, #126 and #127 track other bus-reachable verdict paths.

7. Cost S is optimistic; M is more realistic. It needs a durable inconclusive counter, a new user-facing state, silicon validation of any probe object, changes to host tests that pin `AuthMethodBlocked → PinLocked`, and a CLAUDE.md invariant #2 update.

8. Priority P1, not P0. #104/#105 are labelled priority:high and marked "candidate, source-only, pre-cross-adjudication". The attack needs a physical I2C interposer inside the unit, the outcome is availability loss (funds recoverable from the 24 words; brick permanence is #168), and nothing has shipped.

9. Line drift: the n==2 arm is scp03.rs:615-635 (proposal says 614-634); the `PinLocked` arm is cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-164.

already-have.untracked_delta:
Not tracked in any issue I found:
(a) A typed `Unauthenticated(sw)` result from `unwrap_response`, so callers cannot treat a bare SW as authoritative — #104 only proposes rejecting specific bare SWs.
(b) A consecutive-inconclusive counter on the `CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK` and boot unlock paths that survives a power cycle and escalates to lock, never wipe. The 255a9554 cap is a function-local counter in the PendSV handler; I did not check whether anything persists it.
(c) A distinct user-facing "SE transport fault" state with bounded retry and SE hard-reset.
(d) The R-MAC'd confirmation-probe mechanism itself — see corrections item 3 on whether it closes the attack.
(e) Refreshing #120's body, whose cited global status mapping the driver's doc comment says no longer exists.
